summary: 1935 BC-301 structure on a 30 foot steel tower in Los Padres NF, San Luis Obispo County; last staffed 1992; private land around it; threatened by the 2025 Gifford Fire.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 structure on a 30 foot K-brace open steel tower
facts.status_note: Last visit report in the sources is from 2012; a 2025 post says the Gifford Fire threatened it, and no source read says whether it was damaged

access.note: Register: site completely surrounded by private property and not accessible to the public; the small plot under the tower is Forest Service land

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Los Padres National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1935; a photo credited to the USFS shows the tower under construction c. 1935
July 1936 (Santa Maria Daily Times): lightning, chief cause of the fires, struck the lookout station; building shaken but undamaged
October 1936 (Santa Ynez Valley News): a 24-mile telephone line from Pozo to the lookout station was nearly complete
Thornton's 1986 survey notes the ground cabin as a WWII Aircraft Warning Service built structure
Last staffed in 1992 per logbook entries; the 2012 trip report found observation reports last dated 1992
Trip report April 15, 2012: tower and lookout cabin still standing; lookout cabin shuttered; ground cabin dilapidated
FFLA post dated September 2, 2025: lookout threatened by the Gifford Fire; post does not say whether damaged

notes_for_editor: Access is private land per the Register; the story does not describe any route and advises staying off private land. Height 9.1 m is the 30 foot tower height from the Register description; it is not a total height. The Register's 2019 registration and 2012 trip report agree the tower stood then; the 2025 post reports a threat from the Gifford Fire without saying whether the structure survived, so current condition is unknown. Staffing: last staffed 1992 per logbook; a landowner's account in the trip report is not repeated. The FFLA post is Facebook; its text was read through the post page, not a login. No photos added: the NHLR photos are credited to individuals and USFS, and no image URLs were read.
